newsitem.title: UK: Prince Charles, Diana to improve working ties-paper.
newsitem.headline: Prince Charles, Diana to improve working ties-paper.

text.p: Prince Charles and Princess Diana have agreed to build closer working ties after their bitter divorce last year in a bid to protect the monarchy for their sons, the Sunday Times newspaper said.

It quoted senior royal sources as saying the two might even carry out joint official engagements later in the year, something which would have been dismissed as fanciful not so long ago as the two carried out a protracted sniping war through the media.

If true, the new spirit of cooperation would coincide with increasing doubts about the future of the monarchy. Opinion polls last week showed that 48 percent of the population did not believe the institution would survive the next 50 years.
"(Charles) is concerned about trying to preserve the institution for the next generation," one royal source told the newspaper. The couple have two sons, Princes William, 14, and Harry, 12.
Sources close to Diana told the newspaper that the pair's private offices would coordinate schedules to avoid clashes.
If the couple did decide to bury some of the vindictiveness which has marred their relationship for the last five years it could help boost the damaged image of the prince.
The Daily Mail newspaper said last week that Buckingham Palace expected to mount a five-year campaign to persuade dubious Britons that Charles was fit to be king.
It said the palace took the decision after a television poll showed Charles had slumped in popularity after his acrimonious divorce and affair with old flame Camilla Parker Bowles.

He is being groomed to take over some duties from his 70-year-old mother, Queen Elizabeth, including some of her state visits abroad. He will visit Hong Kong next June, representing the queen when the colony is handed back to China.
